# Example 2 — A canned-data stub made honest

## Before

The generator scaffolds the billing endpoints before the billing work is
scheduled. The stub for one operation is filled with plausible sample data
so the page "works" during a demo:

```ts
// src/api/generated/billing.ts
// @generated by openapi-generator 7.x from api/openapi.yaml — do not edit.
export async function listInvoices(): Promise<Invoice[]> {
  return [
    { id: "inv_001", total: 4900, status: "paid" },
    { id: "inv_002", total: 9900, status: "open" },
  ];
}
```

The billing page renders these as the signed-in customer's real invoices.
The feature is reported complete; the sample records are the only ones any
user ever sees.

## After

Until the operation is implemented, the generated stub fails loudly:

```ts
// src/api/generated/billing.ts
// @generated by openapi-generator 7.x from api/openapi.yaml — do not edit.
export async function listInvoices(): Promise<Invoice[]> {
  throw new NotImplementedError("listInvoices: generated stub, not implemented");
}
```

The billing page cannot ship against this stub — its integration test fails
on the explicit error — and the stub honesty check (G-DX-025) greps
generated operations for canned return bodies. When billing is built, the
real implementation replaces the stub behind the same signature.

Note: corrects DX-049 — an unimplemented generated stub throws an explicit not-implemented error; it never returns canned data that callers or UI can mistake for real behavior.
